title: President Biden signs 95 billion dollar foreign aid package including Ukraine funding
body:
On Wednesday 24 April 2024, U.S. President Joe Biden signed a 95 billion dollar foreign aid bill for Ukraine, Israel and Taiwan. The Senate had passed it 79 to 18 late on Tuesday 23 April, after the House of Representatives approved it by a similarly lopsided margin. The White House had sent its request to Congress in October 2023, and officials said the months-long delay had hurt Ukraine on the battlefield.

The package included 60.8 billion dollars for Ukraine, 26.3 billion for Israel and humanitarian relief including in Gaza, and 8.1 billion for the Indo-Pacific to counter China. The House added language requiring the president to seek repayment from Kyiv for roughly 10 billion dollars in economic aid as forgivable loans, an idea first floated by Donald Trump. The bill also included a provision that could lead to a nationwide ban on TikTok.

House Speaker Mike Johnson had initially refused to bring a Ukraine vote unless it was paired with border measures. After Trump helped derail a bipartisan border bill, Johnson relented and passed the aid with Democratic votes. Shortly after the signing, the Pentagon announced plans to send 1 billion dollars in military aid, including air defence interceptors, artillery rounds, armoured vehicles and anti-tank weapons. Biden called it a "good day for world peace". Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky thanked the Senate.
